name: Rifter Frame Bag
dims_raw: REI: 13.75 x 10 in; bike-packing.de: 349 x 254 mm (L x H); 254 g
dims_note: UNRESOLVED -- the depth is the problem and no source publishes one. Length and height ARE now confirmed: REI's listing for the Rifter gives the four sizes as 13.75 x 10 in, 15 x 11 in, 16 x 12.5 in and 17.25 x 14 in, which convert to 34.9 x 25.4 / 38.1 x 27.9 / 40.6 x 31.8 / 43.8 x 35.6 cm -- the catalogue values to the millimetre -- and states the capacity range as 4.5 to 8.5 L, also matching. So the flagged shortfall is NOT in len, hgt or the litres. It is the 3.8 cm wid, which no maker or retailer publishes and which cannot be reconciled with the rated capacity: BIKEPACKING.com's review says outright that 'the Rifter is wider than most of my custom frame bags and has a moderately flared front', and custom frame bags run 5-6.5 cm. A depth near the Ripio's retailer-published 6.4 cm would bring the box to 1.2-1.3x the litres and resolve the flag, but that is an inference and no source states it, so dims_cm is left exactly as found per the no-fabrication rule. RECOMMENDATION for a future pass: get the depth from Revelate directly; treat 3.8 cm as suspect. Separately, the too-cubic flag on this product is a FALSE POSITIVE for the same reason as the Ripio -- a frame bag cannot be 1.5:1. Note also that two volume sets are in circulation: BIKEPACKING.com's review gives 3.7/4.4/5.7/7.1 L (the launch figures) while REI and the catalogue carry 4.5/5.5/7/8.5 L; the catalogue's are the current ones and are left alone. Revelate blocks bots, so this figure is retailer-sourced (dims_source: retailer) and is weaker evidence than a maker spec block.

name: Cranny Frame Bag
dims_raw: bike-packing.de spec table: "Volume 0.6 liters; Weight 72 g; Dimensions (A / B) 22.9 / 16.5 cm; Width 9.5 cm"
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE on both flags, but it took the photo to see why. assets/products/revelate-designs/cranny-cranny-frame-back-black (local copy cranny-cranny-frame-bag-0-6l-1.jpg) shows a small CRESCENT-shaped wedge with three velcro tabs -- fat and rounded where it meets the head-tube corner and tapering away to nothing along both edges. Its outline fills well under half its own bounding box, and the 9.5 cm width is the MAXIMUM at the fat end, not a uniform thickness. That is the whole explanation for the volume-too-big flag (box 3.6 L against 0.6 L): integrate a wedge that tapers from 9.5 cm to zero over a crescent outline and you land at roughly 0.6-0.7 L. Revelate quotes 38 cu in (0.62 L) and 72 g -- a 72 g bag is not a 3.6 L box. The too-cubic flag fails for the same reason: a corner wedge is not a top-tube sliver and cannot be 2.2:1. All three axes are bike-packing.de's as printed. Revelate blocks bots, so this figure is retailer-sourced (dims_source: retailer) and is weaker evidence than a maker spec block.

name: Joey Downtube Bag
dims_raw: 1 L: 10.2 cm diameter x 17.8 cm length; 109 g
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE (too-cubic, 1.75 against a 1.8 threshold -- a 3% miss). Volume confirms it: pi/4 x 10.2^2 x 17.8 = 1.45 L for a cylinder against a rated 1 L, whereas the square box the checker used is 1.85 L. The 1.8 rule is measuring the aspect of a downtube bottle-bag and the real article is 1.75:1. Revelate blocks bots, so this figure is retailer-sourced (dims_source: retailer) and is weaker evidence than a maker spec block.

Two independent sources agree on the ~10 cm width. Revelate blocks bots, so this figure is retailer-sourced (dims_source: retailer) and is weaker evidence than a maker spec block.

name: Handlebar Bag ADV
dims_raw: Capacity: 19L. Dimensions: length 22cm/8.5" (when the roll top is stretched: 38cm/15"), width 42cm/16.5" (including side pockets), depth 22cm/8.5". Material: Cordura Nylon Fabric
dims_note: DIMS ARE RIGHT, THE SLOT IS WRONG. The photos settle it: assets/products/fairweather/handlebar-bag-handlebar-bag-adv-one-size-19l-1.jpg shows a structured, squared-off rando/porteur box sitting on a front rack with lidded side pockets and a MOLLE-webbed front panel, and -2.jpg shows the strap-to-bar mounting close up. It is not a drybag roll. Every other barroll in this catalogue is a cylinder 40-65 cm long and 15-20 cm in diameter (Sweetroll, Ortlieb Handlebar-Pack, Tailfin, WOHO); a 42 x 26.8 x 22 box is not in that family, which is precisely why the 1.8 elongation check fired at 1.57. Reclassified to barbag, where its nearest neighbour is the Swift Zeitgeist (48.3 x 22.9 x 17.8, 12 L). Dimensions themselves check out against the photo: measuring image 1, total width including side pockets is ~1.6x the body height, matching 42 vs 26.8. Box 24.8 L against a rated 19 L (1.3x), normal for a rolltop measured part-extended. Bluelug's 'length' is the vertical roll dimension (22 cm down, 38 cm stretched), which is why hgt sits between the two.

name: Frame Bag ADV (Medium)
dims_raw: Size small - Capacity: 3.6 liters, Dimension: L 33cm x H 27.5cm x W 6cm. Size medium - Capacity: 4L, Dimension: L 34cm x H 33cm x W 6cm. Weight: 141g (AVG.)
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE on BOTH flags, settled by the two photos. assets/products/fairweather/frame-bag-frame-bag-adv-medium-medium-4l-1.jpg (teal, on a bike) and -2.jpg (coyote, on a green MTB) both show a near-equilateral TRIANGLE hanging from the top tube -- measuring image 1, the bag's top edge and its vertical extent are the same length to within a few percent, which is 34 x 33 exactly as bluelug prints it. (1) too-cubic: the 2.2 elongation rule assumes a framebag_half is a long sliver under the top tube; this one is a full-height front-corner triangle, so 1.03 is the true shape, not a transposition. (2) too-big-for-frame at 33 cm: the photos ARE the disproof -- the bag is mounted on real bikes with a bottle cage still usable below it. A 56cm gravel main triangle is ~45 cm tall at the seat tube, so 33 cm fits with room to spare; the 30 cm cap is too tight. Volume reconciles on the correct triangular basis: 34 x 33 x 6 / 2 = 3.4 L against a rated 4 L, with the bulge making up the difference. Fixed-size zip bag, so L x H x W maps straight across.

dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE (too-cubic, 1.39). Re-fetched the MAKER's own page and the numbers are exact: 50 x 36 x 8 cm for size L, 12 L. WOHO labels the axes L x W x H but their 'W' is the vertical drop and their 'H' the across-bike thickness, so the catalogue's len/hgt/wid mapping is already correct. Same class as the Apidura and Ripio full-frame flags from chunk 1: a bag shaped to a main triangle cannot reach 1.5:1. Box 14.4 L against 12 L is 1.20x -- if anything this is one of the better-reconciled records in the batch. Dims upgraded from unknown to maker-sourced; nothing changed.

name: XTouring UL Pannier Dry
dims_raw: Bikerumor (from WOHO): "Size: 28cm to 49cm tall (depending on roll top), 32cm wide, and 13cm deep. Volume: 36 liters a pair (roll top fully open), 20 liters a pair (rolled three times). Weight: 350g (single), 700g (pair)". BIKEPACKING.com launch: "49cm (full)-35 (rolled 3 times) tall x 32cm wide x 13cm deep"
dims_note: CORRECTED -- the stored 40 x 24 x 14 matched no published axis on this bag and looks back-computed. Two independent press sources working from WOHO's own release agree: 32 cm wide (fore-aft on the rack), 13 cm deep (across the bike), and 28-49 cm tall depending on how far the roll-top is closed, with 35 cm being rolled three times. Recorded as the packed, as-mounted state: len 32, hgt 35, wid 13. On the volume-too-small flag the answer is THE LITRES ARE THE MAXIMUM-ROLL FIGURE: 36 L a pair fully open = 18 L per bag is the catalogue's number and is correct per bag, but it belongs to the 49 cm fully-open height (32 x 49 x 13 = 20.4 L, ratio 1.13). Rolled three times the bag is 14.6 L. capacity_l left at 18 per bag. One outlier noted and rejected: thecyclelist.co lists 8.25 x 5 x 19.25 in (21 x 12.7 x 48.9 cm), agreeing on the 13 cm depth and the 49 cm height but giving 21 cm where both press sources say 32 cm; a 21 cm-wide 18 L pannier is not credible. WOHO's own product URL for this model 404s, so this is press-sourced, not maker-page-sourced.

name: Hoja Handlebar Rolltop
dims_raw: Varuste.net (labelled): "Height: 23 cm / Width: 21 cm / Depth: 22 cm / Volume: 13 l"; Fjallraven and six other retailers: "23 x 21 x 22 cm", 13 L, 395 g
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE -- the bag really is a near-cube and these are Fjallraven's own figures. I went looking for a dropped or duplicated axis and found none: varuste.net publishes the dimensions WITH LABELS as Height 23 / Width 21 / Depth 22, which maps exactly onto the stored len 21 (across the bars) / hgt 23 / wid 22 (fore-aft), and the unlabelled '23 x 21 x 22 cm' is repeated verbatim by Fjallraven, BIKE24, MyFoxBag, Snowleader, MTBIKER and others. The Hoja is a small rolltop cube that mounts on a handlebar RACK rather than spanning the bars, which is why it has none of a barroll's length. One dissenting source, Miyar Adventures (selling the Specialized-branded version), gives 'Height: 23 cm, Width: 31cm, Depth: 22 cm' -- 31 rather than 21 would have been a tidy dropped-digit story and would fix the volume (15.7 L box against 13 L), but it is a single small dealer against the maker and six retailers, so it is rejected and recorded here only so the next pass does not re-derive it. The 10.6 L box against 13 L rated is the rolltop: 13 L is the roll-open figure. It will render as a ball because it is one.

name: Holman Pannier
dims_raw: Chrome spec (via Altitude Sports and Bikeinn, H x W x D): "15.5"x11.5"(Top)-10.75"(Base)x5"", Volume "15-20L", weight 1.1 kg
dims_note: CORRECTED -- MISASSIGNED AXES, the defect the brief warns about. Chrome publishes the Holman as H x W x D = 15.5 x 11.5 (top, tapering to 10.75 at the base) x 5 inches. The catalogue had put the HEIGHT (15.5 in = 39.4 cm) into len and the DEPTH (5 in = 12.7 cm) into hgt, which renders a pannier lying on its side. Correct mapping for a bag hanging off a rack: hgt 39.4 (vertical), len 29.2 (fore-aft, the 11.5 in top edge), wid 12.7 (across the bike). That also resolves the volume-too-small flag for free, and the answer is THE LITRES ARE THE MAXIMUM-ROLL FIGURE: Chrome's own spec is a RANGE, '15-20L', and the box is 29.2 x 39.4 x 12.7 = 14.6 L -- within 3% of the 15 L rolled-down end of Chrome's own range. capacity_l left at the marketed 20 L, which is the roll-open end. Note the fore-aft edge tapers 29.2 cm at the top to 27.3 cm at the base; the larger figure is recorded.

name: Mamquam Frame Bag L/XL
dims_raw: 20" Wide x 9.5" High x 2.25" Deep; 6 Liters
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE (too-cubic, 2.11 against a 2.2 threshold -- a 4% miss). The photo assets/products/two-wheel-gear/mamquam-mamquam-frame-bag-l-xl-l-xl-6l-1.jpg is a clean side-on studio shot of the bag mounted on a bike, and it shows exactly the long low sliver the framebag_half slot expects: measuring it, the bag runs about 2.3x as long as it is tall, which is the stored 50.8 / 24.1 = 2.11 within measurement error and on the correct side of it. Two Wheel Gear print the spec in inches (20 x 9.5 x 2.25) and it maps straight across, 20 in along the top tube and 2.25 in as the across-bike thickness. Box 7.0 L against a rated 6 L (1.16x), consistent with the tapered rear end visible in the photo. This is a threshold that wants relaxing, not a record that wants fixing.

name: Transporter MIK Pannier Bag 30L
dims_raw: Giant: "Size: 30*17*40cm", "Weight: 1400g", "Volume: 30L"; multiple Giant dealers print "Volume: 30L (15L per side)"
dims_note: CORRECTED on two counts, and the photo drove both. assets/products/giant/transporter-transporter-mik-pannier-bag-30l-30l-single-1.jpg and -2.jpg show a DOUBLE pannier -- two bags joined by a saddle panel that drapes over the rack -- and each half is clearly PORTRAIT, measurably about 1.45x taller than it is long. (1) AXIS ORDER. Giant's page gives a bare '30*17*40cm' with no labels, and the catalogue had read the 40 as fore-aft depth, which would make each bag landscape -- the opposite of the photo. Remapped to len 30 (fore-aft along the rack), hgt 40 (vertical), wid 17 (across the bike). 40/30 = 1.33 against the ~1.45 measured off the photo, the difference being the roll top standing proud. A 40 cm fore-aft pannier would also foul the rider's heel; 30 x 40 x 17 is the standard commuter-pannier envelope (cf. Ortlieb Back-Roller at 32 x 42 x 17). (2) CAPACITY. The 30 L is the PAIR, not one bag. Giant dealers print 'Volume: 30L (15L per side)'; MIK ('Mounting Is Key') is a top-of-rack plate system, so a MIK pannier bag is necessarily a two-sided unit rather than a single hanging bag; and 1400 g is a double-bag weight. The catalogue models one side in the pannier slot, so capacity_l is set to 15. That also clears the volume-too-small flag: the per-side box is 20.4 L against 15 L per side, a ratio of 1.36, textbook for a roll-top. Note the size string still reads '30L (single)' and is misleading, but it is the join key so it is left alone.
